A drawback of the NFFRCISTG model described in @sec-network-causal-inference is that it takes the pattern of causal interference as known and fixed. In many settings the network is itself produced by the causal process under study: people choose where to live and whom to visit, and those choices respond to what has happened before. 

In this section of the appendix, we first extend the NFFRCISTG model by allowing the network to be randomly generated by the [causal model](#def-causal-model), which gives the [Random Network FFRCISTG model (RNFFRCISTG)](#def-rnffrcitg). We then allow for two classes of observational unit — people and places — with ties only between people and places, which gives the [Bipartite Random Network FFRCISTG model (BRNFFRCISTG)](#def-brnffrcistg).  It is a [causal model](#def-causal-model) that includes one or more [*graph generators*](#def-npsem-ne) — matrices of relational variables that model the network edges as random variables, one for each ordered pair of observational units, since influence need not run both ways. We also give two restrictions on how people's ties to places form, which make the network's law estimable from one realization: local row formation and, for ties formed dyad by dyad, the [DBRNFFRCISTG](#def-dbrnffrcistg). [Nonparametric identification and estimation](#sec-identification-estimation) uses them.  

Before outlining the [BRNFFRCISTG](#def-brnffrcistg), we introduce new tools -- the causal directed acyclic network graph (DANG), the single world intervention network graph (SWING), and the random network NPSEM.
